title: Structured Care Transitions Protocol
implementation_guidance: Implement a structured care transitions protocol that includes: 1) Initiating contact with patients within 48 hours of hospital discharge; 2) Conducting a comprehensive post-discharge assessment using a standardized tool that evaluates medication understanding, follow-up appointment comprehension, warning signs knowledge, and social support needs; 3) Creating a personalized care transitions plan with specific action items and responsible parties; 4) Scheduling follow-up appointments with primary care within 7 days of discharge; 5) Performing medication reconciliation with teach-back verification; and 6) Implementing a graduated follow-up schedule with contacts at 3, 7, 14, and 30 days post-discharge, with intensity adjusted based on risk stratification. The protocol should include clear escalation pathways for clinical concerns and standardized documentation templates to ensure consistent communication across the care team.
expected_outcomes: Reduced 30-day hospital readmission rates, improved medication adherence, increased attendance at follow-up appointments, earlier identification of post-discharge complications, and enhanced patient satisfaction with care transitions.
target_population: All patients discharged from acute care settings, with particular emphasis on those with complex medical conditions, polypharmacy, or history of readmissions
citation: Coleman EA, Parry C, Chalmers S, Min SJ. The care transitions intervention: results of a randomized controlled trial. Arch Intern Med. 2006;166(17):1822-1828. doi:10.1001/archinte.166.17.1822
